en: The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Questions of Maudgalyāyana,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Imperial Censor and Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial,
the Great Master of the Transmission of the Teaching, the Subject Fata, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard:
At one time the Buddha was staying at the Bamboo Grove Monastery in the city of Rājagṛha.
At that time, in the latter part of the night, the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana went from his own dwelling to the place where the Buddha was.
Having arrived, he prostrated himself on the ground, bowed at the Buddha’s feet, and sat to one side.
At that time, the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana rose from his seat and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If there are bhikṣus or bhikṣuṇīs who, being intoxicated by delusion, violate the precepts, lacking shame and remorse, treating the disciplinary code with contempt, and practicing unrighteous conduct.
World-Honored One!
"How do they come to obtain such merit?
The World-Honored One addressed the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana:

"Suppose there are bhikṣus or bhikṣuṇīs who, being intoxicated by delusion, violate the precepts, lacking shame and remorse, showing contempt for the disciplinary code, and practicing unrighteous conduct."

"When that person’s life ends, they will be reborn in hell. Their lifespan there is equal to five hundred years of the Four Great Kings Heaven; calculated by human reckoning, it is nine million years.
Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

If there are bhikṣus or bhikṣuṇīs who are deluded and intoxicated, violating the precepts, lacking shame and remorse, treating the disciplinary code with contempt, and not relying on the teaching of the Dharma—
how can such persons obtain merit?
The Blessed One addressed the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana:

“If there are bhikṣus or bhikṣuṇīs who, being intoxicated by delusion, violate the precepts, lack shame and dread of blame, treat the disciplinary code with contempt, and do not rely upon the teaching as it was spoken.”
When those people die, they are reborn in hell, where their lifespan is equal to one thousand years of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven; by human calculation, this amounts to thirty-six million years.
The Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If there are bhikṣus or bhikṣuṇīs who, being deluded and intoxicated, violate the precepts, lacking shame and remorse, treating the disciplinary rules with contempt, and committing the *pāyattika* offenses;”
"How do they come to obtain such merit?
The World-Honored One addressed the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana:

"If there are bhikṣus or bhikṣuṇīs who, being intoxicated by delusion, violate the precepts, lacking shame and remorse, and treating the disciplinary code with contempt, commit the *pāyattika* offenses."

When that person’s life ends, they will be born in the hells; their lifespan there is equal to two thousand years in the Yāma Heaven, which, calculated by human reckoning, is fourteen koṭis and four million years.
The Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If there are bhikṣus or bhikṣuṇīs who, being deluded and intoxicated, violate the precepts, lacking shame and dread of blame, and treating the Vinaya with contempt, commit the offense of sthūlātyaya.”
"How do they obtain great benefit?
The Blessed One replied to the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana:
"If there are bhikṣus or bhikṣuṇīs who are intoxicated by delusion and violate the precepts, lacking shame and dread of blame, who treat the Vinaya with contempt and commit thullaccaya offenses."

When that person’s life ends, they are reborn in hell; their lifespan there is four thousand years by the reckoning of the Tuṣita Heaven, which calculates to fifty-seven koṭis and sixty thousand years by human calculation.
The Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If there are bhikṣus or bhikṣuṇīs who, being intoxicated by delusion, violate the precepts, lacking shame and dread of blame, and treating the disciplinary code with contempt, commit a *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense.”
"How do they obtain such great benefit?
The Blessed One replied to the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana:

"If there are bhikṣus or bhikṣuṇīs who, being intoxicated by delusion, violate the precepts, lacking shame and dread of blame, treating the disciplinary rules with contempt, and committing the *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offenses..."

When that person’s life ends, they are reborn in hell, where their lifespan is equal to eight thousand years of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven; by human calculation, this amounts to two hundred thirty koṭis and four million years.
The Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
If there are bhikṣus or bhikṣuṇīs who, being deluded and intoxicated, violate the precepts, lacking shame and remorse, and treating the Vinaya with contempt, commit an offense of pārājika."
"How do they obtain such great benefit?
The Blessed One addressed the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana:

"Suppose there are bhikṣus or bhikṣuṇīs who, being intoxicated by delusion, violate the precepts, lacking shame and dread of blame, treating the Vinaya with contempt, and committing a *pārājika* offense."

When those people die, they are reborn in hell; their lifespan there is sixteen thousand years, equal to the lifespan of the gods of the Heaven of Mastery over Others' Emanations, which, calculated by human reckoning, amounts to nine hundred and fifteen koṭis and six million years.
Having heard what the Buddha had spoken, the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana was filled with great joy; he paid homage and departed.
Thus ends the *Sūtra on Maudgalyāyana’s Questions* spoken by the Buddha.
